### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 79d9c1435586d9b411b51a0ac395ea0c23dc3ddc`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 79d9c1435586d9b411b51a0ac395ea0c23dc3ddc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `372f5c1f1df4131fba7273e175ee95ae6e5145e2` — the merge of head `e285ca09502985b49cddd2bb50a0387a5c4549f1` into base `79d9c1435586d9b411b51a0ac395ea0c23dc3ddc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 372f5c1f1df4131fba7273e175ee95ae6e5145e2 && git checkout 372f5c1f1df4131fba7273e175ee95ae6e5145e2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 79d9c1435586d9b411b51a0ac395ea0c23dc3ddc e285ca09502985b49cddd2bb50a0387a5c4549f1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 79d9c1435586d9b411b51a0ac395ea0c23dc3ddc && git merge --no-ff e285ca09502985b49cddd2bb50a0387a5c4549f1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 79d9c1435586d9b411b51a0ac395ea0c23dc3ddc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 79d9c1435586d9b411b51a0ac395ea0c23dc3ddc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Seat ruling on the new public names in this PR (card #36482). Read at main today and the PR's diff at `a0607f1e`.

1. **Widget `field-history`: accepted.** Precedent: the spec forms' kebab-case widget ids named after what they edit (`related-list-entries`, `key-only-record`, `filter-condition`).
2. **`fieldChangeValuesShown(field, object)` → rename to `resolveFieldHistory(field, object)`.** It answers what the authored `fieldHistory` key resolves to once the type default applies. Precedent: `resolveDisplayField` in the same `@objectstack/spec/data` entry (the effective value of a declared key with its default). Carrying the key's own name lets an author or an AI find the rule from the key.
3. **`NO_LINE_VALUE_FIELD_TYPES` → rename to `FIELD_HISTORY_DEFAULT_OFF_TYPES`.** It is the set of types whose `fieldHistory` defaults to off. The private name it had in `plugin-audit` (`NO_LINE_VALUE_TYPES`) described the audit writer's line, not the key; once public on `@objectstack/spec/data`, the name follows the key.

Rename in the export-origins and api-surface baselines, the changeset and the PR body in the same push. L2 still reviews semantics; this ruling covers names only.

Addendum (head `cdad0018`): the parameter interfaces `FieldHistoryField` and `FieldHistoryObject` that follow the rename are accepted (named after the key, like the function).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a0607f1e7701adc7467cc7f2446d769cc6824183`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field-history-default.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/index.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx

Read for this record: card #36482 (body, 3 comments), PR #36580 (body, 3 comments, net diff against merge-base `06c3e5ac`), the check-runs on the head, and the cited code in the tree at the head (`masked-field-types.ts`, `objectql/src/secret-fields.ts`, `SchemaForm.tsx`, `field.zod.ts`, `object.zod.ts`). The rest of the diff (four test files, the two generated spec baselines, eleven translation bundles, two i18n namespaces) is the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface, `@objectstack/spec/data`: four additions, zero removals (`fieldChangeValuesShown`, `NO_LINE_VALUE_FIELD_TYPES`, `FieldChangeValuesField`, `FieldChangeValuesObject`), all from the new `field-history-default.ts` through one `export *` line in `index.ts`. `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` carry exactly those four. A widening: right. The NAMES are not right on this head, see M1.
- Frontend-safety of the subpath: the new module imports one erased type from `field.zod` and the runtime predicate from `masked-field-types.ts`, which itself imports types only. No schema walker, no node builtin. Right.
- Accept-set of authored metadata: unchanged. `fieldHistory` on a field and on `enable` are still `z.boolean().optional()`; the diff touches no `.zod.ts`. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.
- Form surface: three rows (`field.form.ts` field row, `object.form.ts` `fields` record row, `object.form.ts` `enable` composite row) name `widget: 'field-history'`; the two `object.form.ts` rows drop `type: 'boolean'`. An explicit `fieldSpec.widget` wins in `resolveFieldWidget`, so the widget renders on all three faces. Right. A third-party renderer of these published forms that does not register `field-history` loses the boolean hint on the two object-form rows; the schema node is still boolean, so it degrades to its type inference. Acceptable.
- Writer behaviour (`changeValuesShownFor`): unchanged, verified arm by arm in ④. Right.
- Generated text: the `en` bundle's three help texts are byte-equal to the source rows in `field.form.ts` and `object.form.ts`; `de` and `zh-CN` were read and say the same three things. No disagreement found.
- Check-runs on the head at read time (2026-11-23, two polls): concluded and green are Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Lint and Repo Gates and every Lint shard, Type Check source gates and debt ledger, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build UI Deps. Still in progress with no conclusion: Test Core 1 to 10, Test UI 1 to 16, Build Core, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Type Check workspace, Type Check consumer gates. No run concluded red. The test and type-check verdicts are therefore NOT in hand for this record; the delta round reads them on the new head.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening)

`.changeset/36482-field-history-three-way.md` takes `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n`: the five packages the diff moves, no more and no fewer. Under AGENTS.md (changeset rule: the level follows the Metadata-protocol kind alone, `none` takes `patch`, a non-protocol widening ships `patch`) that is the right level, and Check Changeset concluded success on the head. Both declarations are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset body and agree. The changeset body names the two exports M1 renames, so it moves with that fix.

### ③ Boundary flags

- open_questions 1 (new public names, seat's call): ANSWERED by the seat ruling on the PR, comment 7088708778 (posted 00:53Z, after this head): widget `field-history` accepted; `fieldChangeValuesShown` renamed to `resolveFieldHistory`; `NO_LINE_VALUE_FIELD_TYPES` renamed to `FIELD_HISTORY_DEFAULT_OFF_TYPES`; baselines, changeset and PR body in the same push. The head carries the old names: M1.
- Escalated to the seat: the ruling is silent on the two interfaces `FieldChangeValuesField` and `FieldChangeValuesObject`. They are public too and named after the function being renamed; the dev should not guess. Name them in the same ruling before the rename push.
- open_questions 2 (contract review owed): this record.
- Dev deviation 1 (changeset minor to patch): correct, see ②.
- Dev deviation 2 (shared predicate in spec instead of a UI copy of the type list): the claim comment allowed it ("only if the dev's route shares the no-line type list"), the precedent cited (`isMaskedOnReadFieldType`, same directory, same two-consumer reason) is real, and it removes the drift the card's Notes describe. Accepted.
- out_of_scope_findings (Studio FieldDesigner, ObjectFieldInspector, ObjectSettingsPanel have no `fieldHistory` control; carrier #36290): confirmed by grep at the head, none of the three writes or renders `fieldHistory`. Stays with #36290.
- SQL push-down: no query, no id materialisation, no in-app join in the diff. The writer drops a per-write `new Set(collectMaskedReadFields(objectDef))` for a per-field table lookup. Nothing to flag.

### ④ Design judgment

M1 (must-fix) — The head publishes `fieldChangeValuesShown` and `NO_LINE_VALUE_FIELD_TYPES` on `@objectstack/spec/data`; seat ruling 7088708778 renames them to `resolveFieldHistory` and `FIELD_HISTORY_DEFAULT_OFF_TYPES`. A public spec export cannot be renamed after release without a breaking changeset, so the rename lands before merge: `field-history-default.ts` (and its internal set name and jsdoc links), the `audit-writers.ts` import, call and docblock, the `widgets.tsx` import, call and docblock, the comment in `field.form.ts` that names the function, the `index.ts` comment if it names either, both generated baselines, both test files, the changeset body and the PR body. Rename the two interfaces as the seat rules (see ③). No semantic change is asked for.

N1 (nit) — `field-history-default.ts` module header: "Two classes never show them, whatever the flags say on the field's default: a credential field ... never, and a type in the list only when the field opts in" contradicts itself (the second class does show, with a flag). Say it as the function does: a credential field never; a listed type only with `fieldHistory: true` or `trackHistory: true`. The head moves for M1 anyway, so this can ride.

N2 (nit) — Field-row help text (`field.form.ts`, `object.form.ts` `fields` row): "On also shows a media or JSON field's values" is true, and correctly leaves credentials out, but nowhere says that On does nothing on a credential field. The control offers On on a `secret` or `password` row and the writer then keeps values off (`isMaskedOnReadFieldType` is tested before the `true` arm). `field.zod.ts` says it ("a credential field never shows values"); the help text should carry the same clause. Related: "media, JSON" stands for fourteen types that include `signature`, `code`, `address`, `location`, `vector`, `composite`, `repeater`, `record`. The wording matches the schema's own describe on main and the option label itself is exact per type, so the summary is tolerable.

N3 (nit) — The widget always passes `undefined` for the object. Two cases then differ from the writer. (i) Object writes `enable.fieldHistory: false`: label says Default (On), writer says off; disclosed by "The object's own Field History off wins". (ii) A `password` field on a `managedBy: 'better-auth'` object: label says Default (Off), writer says on (the read-mask exemption); not disclosed. No better-auth object declares a `password`-typed field today (`secret-fields.ts` says so), so no author can meet it now. On the object form the object is in the same document, but `RecordField` hands each row only the row as `formData`, so the widget cannot see it without new plumbing; not owed by this card. Accepted deviation, or a follow-up if (ii) ever becomes reachable.

Checked and holding (the seat's a to f):

(a) Writer equivalence. Old arms in order: object `enable.fieldHistory === false`; no field; field `fieldHistory === false`; `credentials.has(key)`; `fieldHistory === true` or `trackHistory === true`; type in the set. New arms: the same six in the same order. The only rewritten arm is the credential one. Old: key in `collectMaskedReadFields(objectDef)`, which is `def && isMaskedOnReadFieldType(def.type, objectDef.managedBy)` over the own entries of `objectDef.fields`. New: `isMaskedOnReadFieldType(field.type, object?.managedBy)` on the `field` the caller passes. Both callers (`planTrackedLookupReads`, `renderTrackedChangeSummary`) pass `fields[key]` from `getFieldDefs(ctx.object)`, which is `getObjectDef(ctx.object).fields`; the object handed to `changeValuesShownFor` is `getObjectDef(ctx.object)` again. Same definition, same `managedBy`, same predicate. No field's verdict moves: `maskingRule`, `requiredPermissions`, `internal` and `ackPlaintextMasking` were read by neither version (per-reader redaction is elsewhere, as the docblock says); a def without `type` is unmasked and on in both; a non-object def is on in both; a key that resolves only through the prototype has no `type` and is unmasked in both; an extension-added field is in `fields` for both. One difference in principle only: the old credential test read the schema fetched at line 2695 and the new one the map fetched at line 2657, with awaits between; the flag arms already read the earlier map in the old code, so this is not a behaviour change worth a finding. The type list is the same fourteen strings in the same order. The old `typeof field.type === 'string'` guard is subsumed by `Set.has`.

(b) Default label. Field rows: `fieldChangeValuesShown({ type, trackHistory }, undefined)` with `fieldHistory` left out, which is what the function's own doc prescribes for "what does unset resolve to"; `trackHistory: true` on a listed type gives Default (On), as the writer. A row with no type yet gives On; the spec test pins `{}` to true. The `enable` row: its `formData` is the `enable` object (`CompositeField` passes `obj`), which has no `type`, so it resolves to On; the writer turns values off only on a literal `false` there, so "Default is on" is right. Object-level On and Default behave the same at the writer; the text does not claim otherwise.

(c) Default removes the key. Field form: `setField` deletes the key on `undefined`. `fields` record row and `enable` composite: the patch spreads `fieldHistory: undefined` into the row or block, the form's documented clear convention (`SchemaForm.tsx`, the comment above `offerUnset`: "a repeater row keeps an undefined that serialisation drops"), already relied on by the optional enum selects. On and Off write literal `true` and `false`. A stored non-boolean draws as Default, matching the writer's literal-only reads. No UI surface at the head writes `fieldHistory` on save (grep over `ui/packages`); the "written on every save" sentence in the writer docblock is about the field's `trackHistory: false`, and `ObjectFieldInspector` now writes `trackHistory: v || undefined`. Limit of this check: the wire serialisation past `SchemaForm` was not traced; the widget test pins `onChange(undefined)` only at the widget.

(d) Help text. No false sentence found; the gaps are N2 and N3. The `trackHistory` help text is untouched and still true against the predicate (`false` does not hide; `true` opts a listed type in).

(e) Exports. `readonly FieldType[]`, frozen, `satisfies` checks membership at compile time and the test checks it against `FieldType.options` at run time. The function is total over stored metadata (literal-only reads, null object, null field), matching its doc. Names: M1.

(f) Performance: nothing added on the write path.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5df919cb573626c86f200b33648c130a0284c8d3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field-history-default.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/index.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx

Delta round 1 on the at-tier record 7088768550 (head `a0607f1e`, FAIL, M1 open). Read for this record: card #36482 (body, 3 comments), PR #36580 (body, 6 comments, 27-file list), the rework `a0607f1e..5df919cb` whole and per commit (`cdad0018`, `5df919cb`), the four `hits` files and the two implementing files at the head, `masked-field-types.ts` and the `fieldHistory` describe in `field.zod.ts` at the head, and the check-runs on the head (two polls). The rest of the diff (four test files, two generated spec baselines, eleven translation bundles, two i18n namespaces, the changeset prose) is the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface, `@objectstack/spec/data`: still four additions, zero removals against the merge-base `06c3e5ac`, now named `resolveFieldHistory` (function), `FIELD_HISTORY_DEFAULT_OFF_TYPES` (const), `FieldHistoryField` and `FieldHistoryObject` (interfaces). `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` carry exactly those four and none of the old four. A widening: right. The names are the ruled ones (see ③).
- The rework moves no behaviour. Commit `cdad0018` (8 files, 50 lines each way) is identifier substitution only: in `field-history-default.ts` the five arms of the function, their order, the fourteen-type list and its order are untouched; `audit-writers.ts` changes the import, one docblock word and the callee name; `widgets.tsx` changes the import, one docblock word and the callee name, with the same arguments (`{ type, trackHistory }`, `undefined`) and the same `typeof row.type === 'string'` guard; the spec test file changes identifiers only, every expected value is as before. Commit `5df919cb` (14 files) touches one comment paragraph in `field-history-default.ts`, the help-text string of two form rows, and two lines in each of eleven generated bundles. No arm, type list, widget prop, widget id, schema or test expectation moves in either commit.
- Accept-set of authored metadata: unchanged, no `.zod.ts` in the rework. `Metadata-protocol: none` stays right.
- Generated text: the `en` bundle holds the new field-row sentence byte-equal to the source at both places (lines 281 and 914) and the untouched `enable` text byte-equal at line 308. Each of the other ten bundles carries the new clause in both field-row entries; read in `de`, `zh-CN`, `zh-Hant`, `ja-JP`, `ko`, `fr`, `es-ES`, `pt-BR`, `ru`, `ar`, each says a credential field never shows values and keeps the object-off clause.
- Main was not merged in this hop: both rework commits have one parent, the merge-base is still `06c3e5ac`; `origin/main` has moved on to `934ac077`.
- Check-runs on the head (read twice, about 01:01Z to 01:02Z, minutes after the push). Concluded success: Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Auto Label, filter. In progress, no conclusion: both Check Changeset runs, every Lint shard, Type Check source gates, debt ledger, workspace and consumer gates, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards, Flag docs affected. The Test Core and Test UI shards had not been created yet. One PR-body guards run is cancelled, superseded by the later run that concluded success. No run concluded red. The test and type-check verdicts are therefore still NOT in hand on this head either; this record judges the contract as read, and the merge stays behind those gates.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening)

`.changeset/36482-field-history-three-way.md` takes `patch` on the same five packages (`@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n`); the rework touches no sixth package. Its frontmatter is unchanged since the head on which Check Changeset concluded success; on this head the run is still in progress. The body now names `resolveFieldHistory` and `FIELD_HISTORY_DEFAULT_OFF_TYPES`. The PR body and the changeset both carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, line-initial, in agreement. `patch` for a non-protocol widening is the right level.

### ③ Boundary flags

- open_questions 1 (new public names): answered in full. Seat ruling 7088708778 rules the widget id, the function and the const; its addendum (head `cdad0018`) accepts `FieldHistoryField` and `FieldHistoryObject`, "named after the key, like the function". The escalation of the previous record is thereby closed; no name on the head lacks a ruling.
- open_questions 2 (contract review owed): this record, on this head.
- Dev deviations 1 and 2 and the out_of_scope_findings entry (carrier #36290): judged in 7088768550, nothing in the rework reopens them.
- New in the lane's account: N3 recorded as an accepted deviation in the PR body's Acceptance notes. Read there; the note states both differing cases and why the second is unreachable today. Accepted as written.
- SQL push-down: the rework adds no query, no id materialisation, no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

M1: closed — `git grep` over the whole tree at the head finds none of `fieldChangeValuesShown`, `NO_LINE_VALUE_FIELD_TYPES`, `NO_LINE_VALUE_FIELD_TYPE_SET`, `FieldChangeValuesField`, `FieldChangeValuesObject`, nor the old private `NO_LINE_VALUE_TYPES`. The rename covers the module (export, internal set, jsdoc links), the writer's import, call and docblock, the widget's import, call and docblock, the `field.form.ts` comment, both baselines, the spec test file, the changeset body and the PR body (which names the old private set once, correctly, as the thing removed). `index.ts` named neither. The interfaces carry the ruled names.

N1: closed — the module header now reads as the function does: a credential field never shows values whatever its flags say; a type in the list shows them only with `fieldHistory: true` or `trackHistory: true`. Checked against the arms: the mask test precedes the two `true` tests, and the list is consulted last.

N2: closed — both field rows (`field.form.ts`, the `fields` row of `object.form.ts`) now end "A credential field never shows values, and the object's own Field History off wins." True against the code: `isMaskedOnReadFieldType` returns before the `true` arm, so On does nothing on a `secret` or a generic `password`. It is the same sentence as the `fieldHistory` describe in `field.zod.ts`. Its one inexact case is a `password` on a `managedBy: 'better-auth'` object, which the mask exempts and which therefore does show; that is N3 case (ii), unreachable today. The second half of the previous note (media, JSON standing for fourteen types) is unchanged and was already judged tolerable.
